items.subject: DiscreteInteger
notes: User-supplied spec: three equivalent characterizations of Z -- (1) two-sided Peano/System SP (0, Succ, Pred, invertibility, acyclicity, bidirectional induction), (2) free infinite cyclic group (universal algebra view), (3) discretely ordered ring / Presburger completeness. The six pre-existing independent classes (HasSuccessor, HasPredecessor, SuccessorLaws, SuccessorAdditionLaw, SuccessorMultiplicationLaws, DiscretenessLaw) already correspond to definition (1) plus a bridge to (3)'s ring structure; kept that shape per D6, did not attempt to also build out (2)'s free-group presentation or (3)'s full Presburger quantifier-elimination content -- out of scope, new math beyond an audit/reorg pass.

AUDIT BUG FOUND AND FIXED (D2 risk, on this item too): DiscretenessLaw's SuccAperiodic field was quantified only at the basepoint (SuccIterate n (0:R) != 0), not universally as the user's own acyclicity axiom states (forall x, forall n>0, S^n(x) != x). The narrower statement typechecked and looked plausible but is strictly weaker/different -- without extra additive structure nothing forces the basepoint's aperiodicity to transfer to every other element. Fixed: SuccAperiodic (both the class field and its Wrappers-section restated theorem) now quantifies over an explicit x : R matching the spec verbatim. SuccInjective/PredInjective in SuccessorLaws were also reviewed -- these ARE provable consequences of the two invertibility fields rather than independent axioms, but are true and kept as bundled fields for interface convenience, not a bug (noted in the new doc comment).

Reorg: Definition.lean + Laws/Definition.lean (six classes + a Wrappers section of restated theorems, all already sorry'd pre-session) relocated into Interface/{Definitions,Laws}, matching the rest of the tree. DiscreteInteger kept as ONE Laws/Definition.lean file (not split per-class into separate files) since the six classes were already coexisting in one file with no issues -- matches Archimedean's single-file precedent for a subject with no single combining law.

ConceptSignature (Interface/Definitions/ConceptSignature.lean) still extends RingConceptSignature (tier 5's Ring) -- a UA-signature-level dependency, not a Laws-level one, so it doesn't affect D5's tier ordering (which only tracks Laws/Definition.lean imports) or block this item from being tier 1. Left as-is, pre-existing, not touched beyond the folder move -- flagged here as a known oddity worth a second look whenever Ring (as-24) itself gets reorged.

No Constructions/ folder built this item, unlike every prior item -- HasSuccessor/ HasPredecessor/DiscretenessLaw are LRA-specific classes with no single matching generic Mathlib typeclass to bridge from (unlike Group/SemilatticeSup/Archimedean's 1-1 Mathlib counterparts); Z is also essentially the *only* model per the user's own categoricity framing, so a generic multi-carrier bridge wouldn't buy much. items.subject: JoinSemilattice
notes: D6 resolved (important, see DECISIONS.md): the flat def-with-explicit-operation-argument style is DELIBERATE, not a lapse to fix toward class-based [Mul R] uniformity. Lattice needs join AND meet as two independent operations coexisting on one carrier at once, which a single instance-per-type typeclass parameter cannot express. Converting JoinSemilattice to [Mul R] style would have broken Lattice. Kept the style, just relocated into Interface/{Definitions,Laws}.

Audited: JoinSemilatticeLaws = Associative + Commutative + Idempotent on the explicit `join` operation, exactly matching the user's algebraic definition (equivalently, an idempotent commutative semigroup). A separate, pre-existing order-theoretic definition lives at LRA.Order.Lattices.JoinSemilattice (poset+suprema) — no bridge between the two exists yet, flagged as future Interop work, out of scope for this reorg pass.

Constructions/Mathlib/Laws.lean: ofSemilatticeSup, a plain theorem (not an instance!) that [SemilatticeSup R] gives JoinSemilatticeLaws (·⊔·) — safe because it never touches Mul/Add at all, so none of the usual instance-diamond risk applies here.

Examples/: UnionSemilattice (Set union, direct), RealsUnderMax (ℝ max, via the Mathlib bridge) — both prove the explicit-function form directly, no wrapper structs needed since there's no Mul-instance to avoid colliding with.
Import-path fix: Lattice/Laws/Definition.lean, VolumeVICore.lean (.Laws -> .Interface.Laws)

items.subject: Lattice
notes: User-supplied spec: order-theoretic (poset where every pair has both a join and a meet) and algebraic ((L,v,^) with idempotent, commutative, associative laws for each of v/^, plus mutual absorption) definitions, confirmed equivalent. Standard examples: power sets under union/intersection, divisibility on positive integers (lcm/gcd), any total order (max/min).

Audited: LatticeLaws join meet := JoinSemilatticeLaws join /\ MeetSemilatticeLaws meet /\ MutualAbsorptionLaw join meet -- unfolding MutualAbsorptionLaw (AbsorptionLaw join meet /\ AbsorptionLaw meet join, i.e. (forall x y, join x (meet x y) = x) /\ (forall x y, meet x (join x y) = x)) confirms this is EXACTLY the user's four algebraic identities: idempotent+commutative+associative for join (from JoinSemilatticeLaws), same for meet (from MeetSemilatticeLaws), and both absorption laws. No gap, no fix needed -- just relocated with a real doc comment.
